title: 6.9.10 Lab: Light the grid
description: An 8 by 8 grid of lights kept as data. The starter has the canvas, the draw loop and the words, and every function you need is there but empty. Build the grid, draw it from the data, flip a cell on a click, and count the lit cells.

steps.title: Build the grid
steps.instructions:
The grid is `grid[r][c]`: `true` when that cell is lit. `COLS` (8), `ROWS` (8) and `CELL` (50) are at the top of the starter, and `setup()` already calls `makeGrid()` and keeps what it gives back in `grid`. Besides `setup()`, `draw()` and `drawTop()`, the starter has four functions, and each is empty or gives back a stand-in until you write it: `makeGrid()` gives back an empty list, `drawGrid()` and `clickCell()` do nothing, and `countLit()` gives back 0. Right now the screen is blank and the words say `lit: 0 of 64`.

Start with `makeGrid()`. It makes `g` for you. Make `ROWS` rows: for each one make an empty array called `row`, push `COLS` values of `false` into it (every light starts off), then push the finished row onto `g`. The whole row goes onto `g` as one item, as in 6.9.9. Nothing shows yet; the next step draws it.
hints: Two loops, one inside the other: the outer makes a row, the inner fills it. `row.push(false);`
`g.push(row);` goes after the inner loop, inside the outer one.

steps.title: Draw it from the data
steps.instructions: In `drawGrid()`, visit every cell with two loops (use `grid.length` and `grid[r].length` as the limits). Before each cell, set `fill`: `'gold'` for a lit cell and `'#334'` for an off cell, chosen by what `grid[r][c]` holds. Then draw the cell with `rect(c * CELL, r * CELL, CELL, CELL)`. A `rect`'s x and y is its top-left corner, so the cell in column `c` starts at `c * CELL`. Run it: an 8 by 8 board of dark squares appears with thin black lines between them. Nothing is lit yet, because every cell is `false`.
hints: `fill(grid[r][c] ? 'gold' : '#334');` or an `if`/`else` that calls `fill` in each branch.
Row `r` goes with y, column `c` goes with x: `rect(c * CELL, r * CELL, CELL, CELL);`

steps.title: A click flips a cell
steps.instructions: `draw()` already calls `clickCell(mouse.x, mouse.y)` on every click. In `clickCell(x, y)`, turn the pixels into a column and a row: `c` is `floor(x / CELL)` and `r` is `floor(y / CELL)`. Then, IF that row and column are on the grid, flip the cell: `grid[r][c] = !grid[r][c];`. The canvas is 440 tall, but the grid is only 400 of it. The strip under the grid is where the words live, and a click there gives row 8, which does not exist: `grid[8]` is `undefined`, and reading a cell of it stops the sketch. So check `r >= 0 && r < ROWS && c >= 0 && c < COLS` first, with the row tests ahead of anything that reads `grid[r]`. Run it: click a few squares to light them, click one again to turn it off, and click in the strip under the grid to check that nothing happens and nothing breaks.
hints: The test and the flip go together: `if (r >= 0 && r < ROWS && c >= 0 && c < COLS) { ... }`
The flip is one line, and `!` turns `true` into `false` and `false` into `true`.

steps.title: Count the lit cells
steps.instructions: In `countLit()`, `n` starts at 0 and is given back at the end for you. Between those, use two loops over the grid and add 1 to `n` for every cell that is `true`. The words under the grid should now count as you click: light three squares and they read `lit: 3 of 64`, turn one off and they read 2.
hints: Same two loops as `drawGrid()`, with `if (grid[r][c]) n += 1;` inside.
A `true` cell is enough for an `if` on its own; there is no need to compare it with anything.
